Unit Capacity: %+n%\\nGuard Corps Soldiers, Banner Troops

This unit consists of statue-warriors forged by Zhen Dan craftsmen. They typically move slowly, but possess higher [[img:ui/skins/default/icon_stat_armour.png]][[/img]]Armour and Mass than regular units, along with substantial resistance to magic and fire, and are unaffected by [[img:icon_morale]][[/img]]Morale or [[img:ui/battle ui/ability_icons/fatigue_immune.png]][[/img]]Fatigue in battle. Zhen Dan's master artisans can repair and further reinforce these units during combat.
This unit hails from the nomadic tribes of northern Zhen Dan. Its morale-affecting effects only apply to other Hu Tribesmen units

This unit is one of the many Imperial Guard forces stationed across Zhen Dan, possessing extremely high [[img:icon_melee_attack]][[/img]]Melee Attack and [[img:icon_melee_defence]][[/img]]Melee Defence, and typically bears a unique weapon enchantment effect

This unit is one of the legendary great beasts of Zhen Dan. These semi-divine creatures possess extremely high [[img:icon_melee_attack]][[/img]]Melee Attack and [[img:icon_melee_defence]][[/img]]Melee Defence, can inflict [[img:ui/battle ui/ability_icons/causes_terror.png]][[/img]]Terror upon enemies, and wield exceptionally powerful special abilities
The unit can switch formations to adapt to different situations
Endless Spirit Puppets, the Calamity Ceases
Guardian War God of the Nation
Hundred Birds Homage to the Phoenix
These orc warriors, who dwell in secluded mountains and forests, have honed their swordsmanship to perfection. They sweep through enemy ranks like an autumn gale.
The White Tiger's ferocity cows the enemy and rallies the three armies.
The Genwuan Yuan Ying are the guardians of the people of Zhen Dan, barring every manner of demon and specter from their door.
Even the Buddha's chant carries a hero's spirit; all martial arts under heaven trace their roots to Shao Lin.
Only when the six roots are purified can the foundation of sagehood be laid; only when the five aggregates are emptied can one speak of the way of benevolence and righteousness.
The bell of the ancient temple's purple bamboo tolls; they walk the martial world to subdue demons and vanquish evil.

The Tide-Washing Court is the mightiest force along the Celestial Empire's vast coastline. They are champions selected by Ming Long through years of endless war, and have forged a battle style all their own in the ceaseless struggle against coastal incursions.
To mortal eyes, the Palace Guard soldiers appear as gods incarnate.

Wrath bristles my hair against my cap, as I lean on the rail; the fierce rain has just ceased.\\n\\nI raise my eyes to gaze afar, and let loose a long howl to the sky, my heart ablaze with fervent resolve.
Members of the Ceremonial Guard Office strike distant targets with specialized weapons, binding them and rending their flesh with concealed mechanisms.

Nan Gau is the forging heart of all Zhen Dan, where tens of thousands of craftsmen toil day and night to supply the empire with divine weapons. As the final line of defense guarding the Ninth Wall, the Rampart Iron Guard's armor and arms are the very finest that Zhen Dan can produce.
Suan Ni is a guardian beast of the sacred order; no evil, however cunning, dares to contend with it.
Bird-like in form, it wields the power to summon thunder and unleash lightning. Wherever it appears, thunderclaps crash in its wake, and all who witness it are struck with dread.
The Forest Wanderer never parts with his wine; the mere scent of liquor about him is enough to leave onlookers reeling drunk.
The Jade Blood Sovereigns are statues of heavenly kings that guard Daoist temples, their jade-carved bodies storing vast reserves of the Winds of Magic.

The golden armor of the Dragon Emperor's Guard is the crystallization of Zhen Dan's supreme forging craft and the power of the Dragon Emperor. These magnificent suits of armor are as unbreakable as Zhen Dan itself.

Women form a vital part of Zhen Dan's armies. Though countless heroines have been immortalized in history, only a rare few are chosen by the Moon Empress. Those selected are summoned to her courtyard, where they receive her blessing before setting out across Zhen Dan to save the common people in her name.
The White-Plumes wear cloaks shed from the flawless hide of the guardian beast of the northern frontier, and blessed further by the Moon Empress, they possess incredible resistance to weapon strikes.

The Vermilion Bird is the most active of the three guardian beasts, and its worship flourishes throughout the southern provinces. The Beacon-Keepers are Li Dao's most loyal inner guards and the Vermilion Bird's most fervent devotees. Amidst the sharp-eyed vigilance of the southern frontier, their twin flaming whips shine brighter than all but the flames of the guardian itself.

The Jade Attendants stand watch over the boundless fertile plains of Zhen Dan, the power of the Winds of Magic surging within their chests. Their proud roar alone is enough to send invading scoundrels quaking with terror.
You gave me the wutong tree; I give you loyalty and valor in return.\\n\\nI shall not fail this body, nor fail you, my lord — I repay my confidant with death in battle.
The heavenly king's wrath thunders forth; his war-axe brings swift judgment and death.
The heavenly king's benevolence spans north and south alike; the righteous path returns once more in majesty.

The armor of the Raven-Feather Legion is layered with demon-repelling feathers refined by alchemists, aiding them in hunting down the practitioners of heretical arts hidden deep within the Zhen Dan Empire.
The tortoise's breath knows no decay; eternal life everlasting.
One body has fought across three thousand li; one blade has once held back a million-strong host.
One of the Moon Empress's powers is healing, and her followers are meant to carry out her will, doing everything in their power to save the common people.
Their second life is soon to fade, but even as their bronze forms crumble to ruin, the heroic spirits within will fight to their last strength to defend home and country.

The Moon God Court is the most unique of the Celestial Court's guard units, usually serving as the Moon Empress's handmaidens, practicing archery alongside her. When summoned to battle, the arrows of these blessed maidens are sharp enough to extinguish the sun itself in the Moon Empress's name.

As the pillar that coordinates all four quarters, the soldiers of the Jade Court excel in coordinated warfare; the Decree Guard's unspoken understanding with one another leaves even other palace guards struggling to keep pace.
The divine bird draws in the primal essence of the heavens to achieve true enlightenment, leading the three armies as their vanguard.
Hammer strikes ring out, forging lightning and embedding shock; the echo carries a thousand miles, shaking heaven and earth.
With every breath, wine transforms into flame, burning away all wickedness.
The crimson phoenix cries out long and clear, and all birds bow before it in submission.
Throughout Zhen Dan's history, countless heroes have risen. Craftsmen have poured the wills of these fallen spirits into statues that guard the land.

Several palace guard formations of differing organization exist throughout the Zhen Dan Empire. Such units typically serve as the imperial guard of various courts, such as the White-Plumes who defend the Bin Tie Court. Members of the palace guard are all exceptional talents of Zhen Dan, and their eternal and singular mission is to protect the safety of the Empire.
Drunk, we lie upon the battlefield—laugh not, my friend; since ancient times, how many who marched to war have returned?
The blade's edge becomes a white shadow; its rainbow glow guards the three armies.
The mortal shell must wither, its earthly bonds spent; the endless spirit puppets—the calamity ceases.

These orc warriors from the south are rumored to be transformed followers of the Dragon Emperor's direct line. They serve as the Empire's claws, using their consummate skill in arms to crush the Empire's enemies.
With the Zhan Ma sword breaking the enemy lines and claiming first blood, none but the Tiger Warriors could be so bold and fierce.
In green robes and flowing silk, sleeves and swords dance; a spear of blossoms, fireflies scattering, cuts down treachery.
In brocade robes and black cloaks, they crush the fiends; with Hong Wu's blue steel, they slay the disloyal.
Iron and fire drive out treachery; beacon smoke stands watch over the nine borders.
Clad in my armor of war, a heroine's bearing shines to all four corners.
Divine might, vivid and unyielding, guards the mortal world; flowing embers, towering high, return to the summit's capital.

The lands north of Chang Yuan lie shrouded beneath the shadow of malevolent spirits. Across this vast wasteland roam countless tribes—though most known khans worship dark powers, many herders merely follow their leaders blindly. South of the wasteland, some gentler tribes maintain close ties with the Celestial Court, and Zhen Dan's frontier armies can often hire these fierce warriors cheaply to serve the Empire. But maintaining a legion beyond the Empire's authority for the long term will surely demand a far steeper price.

The Bronze Cannons have endured through nearly as many ages as Chang Yuan itself. These great guns were cast in the era when the Dragon Emperor still walked among mortals, forged to contend with unspeakable colossal beings that could rival gods. Restored by the artisans of Nan Gao, they march to war once more to bathe Zhen Dan's great enemies in blood.
A blade like a feather, its gleaming edge steals life.
Golden armor and silver trappings wield the halberd beneath the sun; no phantom or specter can escape the iron hooves.
Azure light beneath the sun brings forth thunder; iron rain like pear blossoms blankets the towering sky.
Azure light beneath the sun brings forth thunder; iron rain like pear blossoms blankets the towering sky.
Beyond the broken bridge, raven feathers appear; fallen blossoms drip blood upon the ruins.
One body has fought across three thousand miles; one sword once held back a million-strong army.
Golden armor and silver trappings wield the halberd beneath the sun; no phantom or specter can escape the iron hooves.

[[img:icon_yang]][[col:white]]Unlock method: Complete the unit's quest[[/col]]\\n\\nIn the northern reaches of heaven, seven mansions bear the mark of Yin. Xuan Wu, turtle and serpent entwined as one, was commanded by the Dragon Emperor to guard the North.
Bow drawn beside the moon, the arrow points to a shooting star.

[[img:icon_yang]][[col:white]]Unlock method: Complete the unit's quest[[/col]]\\n\\nIn the western reaches, metal's essence of Xin transforms the Five Elements, giving rise to the White Tiger, forever standing between Heaven and Earth, commanded by the Dragon Emperor to pacify the West.
Amid the vast wilds and mountains, the valiant hold to righteousness; though far from the Heavenly Palace, the Dragon-kin's devotion never fades.

Guard Corps Soldiers are the elite of Zhen Dan's various courts. Unlike national armies such as the Jade Bravos or the Celestial Court's Dragon Guard, the Guard Corps is raised by local authorities, closer in nature to a general's private retainers. Under generals loyal to the Celestial Court, they are the most reliable bulwark protecting the realm and its people; but under warlords who carve out their own domains, they become the force most feared by the imperial armies.
Beyond the frontier, they wish only to return wrapped in their own shrouds; why should the Pacifier of Distant Lands ever return alive through the pass?
A thousand years of history may forget their names in shame, yet their loyal hearts repay the Dragon Emperor all the same.
Upon the Suan Ni's throne, the lion speaks its words; beneath the dust of the Celestial Court, the mortal world sings its praise.
In crimson robes they draw the bow, long sleeves dancing; amid the forest of spears, a cold gleam surges forth.
One hears the tongues of fire but sees not their bearer; in iron robes like fireflies, they offer up their loyal hearts.
A frown, a word, half-veiled behind a fan; a paper parasol, an iron rain, sheltering the fair one.

The monks of Zhen Dan deeply understand the harmony of Yin and Yang. Through ascetic practice, they temper body and mind, aiding the common people through righteousness, and stepping forward whenever the nation calls.
The war chariot is yoked, charging forth to seize the first advantage.
Drunk on the boundless spirit of heroes, they devour the exhilarating winds of all Nine Provinces.

[[img:icon_yang]][[col:white]]Unlock method: Complete the unit's quest[[/col]]\\n\\nCountless tribes of demihumans, vastly different from those of the Old World, are scattered around the Zhen Dan Empire. Those tribes near Zhen Dan have, for the most part, gratefully submitted to the Dragon Emperor's banner—though their kind differs, they stand as close as brothers, guarding eternal peace together.
A heroine rides a hundred miles without pause; a single glance, a single word, bound to the fate of all under heaven.

[[img:icon_yang]][[col:white]]Unlock method: Complete the unit's quest[[/col]]\\n\\nIn the southern reaches, Yang stirs, and the parasol tree grows; the vermillion phoenix cries long, and all birds bow before it, commanded by the Dragon Emperor to govern the South.
The Hong Wu Overseers command the imperial escort, patrols, and arrests, serving as the Dragon Emperor's eyes and ears — no clue, however faint, escapes their discerning gaze.
The Supreme Ultimate gives birth to Yin and Yang; Yin and Yang give birth to the Four Symbols; the Four Symbols give birth to the Eight Trigrams. Such is the natural order, cycling on without end.
The Crossbow Cavalry are charging — soldiers of Zhen Dan, the battle has begun!

Founded during the first northern campaign, the Guan Ning Crossbow Cavalry are Chang Yuan's most elite cavalry force. Independent of all other garrisons, they answer only to the commander of Chang Yuan, trampling the northern wastelands beneath their hooves.
Suan Ni is a guardian beast that gathers the spiritual energies of heaven and earth, aiding in the concentration of Daoist power.

The Cloud Cauldron Strongman hails from the western mountains, the last echo of an ancient age—his people have long since become withered bones in the Valley of Titans. Even the surviving Dragon-kin cannot say for certain just how long this mountain-like giant has spent in Zhen Dan. But they know this: as the Dragon Emperor's ancient ally, the Cloud Cauldron Strongman will fight for Zhen Dan just as he always has.
The strongman stands mighty and unyielding, overturning mountains and seas; a single warrior holds the pass, and ten thousand armies cannot pass.
The tremendous power of the bronze cannon fires shells directly at the enemy, at a speed so great that even the great beasts that once ravaged ancient Zhen Dan could scarcely react in time
The bronze cannon's ingenious design allows its crew to load multiple shells at once, delivering blanket bombardment through lobbed fire

As the group with the highest mastery of the life-aspected Winds of Magic in Zhen Dan, the Jade Blood Daoists mostly gather at the Weng Chang spirit sanctum to cultivate their arts in seclusion. As the Jade Blood Clan grows ever more rampant, the common people and officials of Zhen Dan increasingly turn to them, entreating them to leave their retreat and purge the calamitous spirits and monstrous forces plaguing the land. Yet in the eyes of some, the Jade Blood Clan itself is the very calamity the Jade Blood Daoists once summoned.
The Jade Blood Daoist wields uncanny secret arts, compelling the corpses of those who died far from home to rise and walk again.

[[img:icon_yang]][[col:white]]Unlock method: Complete the unit's quest[[/col]]\\n\\nXingtian once contended with the Dragon Emperor for supremacy. The Emperor severed his head and buried it at Kun Lan. Across ten thousand years, protected by the Dragon's arts and drawing in the essence of heaven and earth, he was reborn—his nipples became his eyes, his navel his mouth, and he dances still, wielding shield and axe.
Xingtian dances with shield and axe; his fierce will endures unbroken.

Zhao Ming's keen fascination with the novelties of mortal men is well known throughout Zhen Dan. Though he firmly believes his own mastery of craft far surpasses that of the common folk of the Old World, his failed attempt to replicate the Empire's steam tanks only deepened his curiosity toward the western realms. Establishing a new army clad in Imperial-style armor was but another such experiment.

Deeply versed in the harmonious laws of metal and stone, the Jade Stone Guards are the Jade Court's most trustworthy protectors. Yuan Bo's enchantments imbue their jade armor with formidable magic resistance—even confronted with terrifying spells capable of rending the earth asunder, the wearers of jade armor remain unshaken.

The world north of Chang Yuan means only formless chaos and death to the common folk of Zhen Dan. But for the Gale Frontier Army, who have fought beyond Chang Yuan for so long, endless war has forged chaos and death into the very substance of their lives.
The unit can only advance slowly
Actively attacking the enemy will break formation, but you can still initiate an attack by moving toward the target

The armor of the Jade Stone Guard is forged from enchanted jade. This peculiar armor not only resists magical attacks but also absorbs the power of the Winds of Magic, periodically deflecting blade damage.

[[img:icon_yang]][[col:white]]Unlock method: Complete the unit's quest[[/col]]\\n\\nHou Xi was once among the many great beasts of Zhen Dan who struggled against the Heavenly Dragon Emperor. Like the other surviving beasts, she was subdued by the Dragon Emperor after the great war, and earned his forgiveness through a blood oath to protect Zhen Dan forever.
White Mother of the Jade River

Hou Xi contended with Hao Tian for supremacy, and in her fury unleashed the waters of the Jade River, snapping the pillar of heaven and severing the cords of earth. Thus the Jade River winds through nine bends and a hundred turns, and all the rivers of the world flow back into her.

The abundant Winds of Magic in Zhen Dan have allowed certain creatures to transcend the limits of their birth and become something far greater — it is believed that Hou Xi and Zhen Dan's other great beasts belong to this rare breed. Hou Xi can summon an endless tide of serpents, protecting her comrades and tearing into her foes.

The Zhe Chong Palace Guards wear magnificent armor and often appear before the common people as the honor guard of the Dragon-kin. Every Zhen Dan soldier who spots the Zhe Chong Palace Guards on the battlefield feels their spirits lift and rushes to prove their valor, for they know it means one of Zhen Dan's most illustrious figures has come to the front lines in person.
By the Dragon's wrath alone, a myriad armies would gladly march to their deaths toward the towering heavens.

The Spirit Qi Lin longs for its homeland at Tian Shan, unable to forget its attachment even amid the ranks of battle and the throes of slaughter. Only through the Sacred Yang Rite can it be made to obey its rider's will.
Hailing from the southeast of Sheng Jiang, the Tiger-Crowned Honor Guards are masters of jungle warfare, hunters more lethal than the tigers themselves.
The tiger's roar strikes fear into all who hear it, yet even more fearsome than any beast is this martial officer.

Sun and moon forever hang above the loyal and valiant heart; wind and dust are cast aside from the eyes that see through wickedness.

These ogres from the Long-Tusk Road are held in high favor by Zhao Ming, and the mightiest among them are summoned into his hall. In times of peace, these powerful strongmen compete in Shang Yang's arenas as champions of the Bin Tie Court, crushing any foe bold enough to stand against them with overwhelming might.
The Daoists of Zhen Dan seal the power of the Winds of Magic into talismans, to be used in times of need

The Celestial Masters open their ritual, offering their own life force as the price to briefly summon back a fragment of the Soul Dragon's spirit to the battlefield.
The Soul Dragon is the daughter of the Heavenly Dragon Emperor, forever asleep beneath the waters. Lost souls follow her dreams to their final resting place.
The Soul Dragon's spirit wails at the sight of fallen warriors, and heaven and earth tremble in response; even the winds of Sha Xu cannot bear to carry away her people this day.

Legend holds that the extraordinary power of the Dragon Emperor's Guard was personally bestowed by the Vast Dragon centuries ago, making them unmatched in strength. But with the Dragon Emperor's passing, the Celestial Court's guard can no longer draw fresh blood into its ranks. These last hundred-odd guardsmen are the final legacy of that ancient blessing — should even they fall in battle, the name of the Dragon Emperor's Guard will fade into nothing more than another half-forgotten legend of Zhen Dan.
Only a scarce few units can use abilities of this kind.

The arrows of the Moon God Court are woven from the shadows cast by the Moon Empress herself; so long as the veiled magical winds continue to blow, the arrows of these spell-weaving maidens shall never run dry.
The White Elephant King's trunk is as agile and unstoppable as a flood dragon. When you see its trunk sweeping toward you on the battlefield, close your eyes tight and start praying.
The White Elephant King's trunk gathers unmatched power, coiling around its foes to twist and crush them to death.
Hammer strikes ring out, forging lightning and embedding shock; the echo carries a thousand miles, shaking heaven and earth.
The earth trembles with every step of the White Elephant King; lesser creatures cannot even find their footing before it, let alone stand and fight.
Roar!\\nAfter years of research, a Zhen Dan linguist has concluded that this cry means, "Good wine, more please!"
The power of Marshal Tian Peng comes from the Five Elements Compass of Wei Jing; so long as the compass's power continues to turn, Marshal Tian Peng draws upon an endless font of vitality.
Daemonic units will take additional damage

[[img:icon_yang]][[col:white]]Unlock method: Complete the unit's quest[[/col]]\\n\\nThe Overseer of the Heavens was born of the Winds of Magic, a divine general created personally by the Dragon Emperor to oversee both heaven and the mortal realm. Legend holds that, at the Dragon Emperor's command, he once beheaded a rebellious Dragon-kin and took its claw as a trophy—only to slit his own throat under the crushing weight of his guilt for slaying one of his own kind. The Dragon Emperor then grafted the rebel's claw onto the Overseer's bleeding neck, and as the Winds of Magic surged into him, he was reborn. No one knows whether any trace of the Overseer's own will still lingers beneath that dragon claw; all that people see is the Overseer forever carrying out the Dragon Emperor's will, purchasing Zhen Dan's lasting peace with blood. Before departing, the Dragon Emperor sent the Overseer to Tian Shan. Some say he went to watch over the demons south of the mountain; others say he was set to guard, for a thousand years, over the punished Monkey-Head. But since then, no one has ever seen the Overseer of the Heavens again. People still believe that though he has no eyes, his spiritual power watches over every corner of Zhen Dan—and should the realm ever face true crisis again, he shall return to fly once more among mortals.
With Wind Fire Wheels beneath his feet, he moves freely across the battlefield, tongues of flame dancing in his wake.
The Winds of Magic surge forth, forming an impassable firestorm around him — face true power, if you dare.
With a single mystic gesture, he commands flame to strike down his enemies.
With sword planted against the earth, good fortune grows and the roots of calamity are severed.
Heavenly King Duan Wang releases the vital energy stored within his gourd, granting a boon to his allies.
As the heavenly king plucks his pipa, countless spiritual energies surge forth from its strings, coalescing into weapons that strike down his enemies.
Wind and rain gather beneath Heavenly King Wen Chen's treasured umbrella, awaiting only the moment he unfurls it to summon storm and downpour.

This unit is one of the Four Heavenly King Statues of Zhen Dan, guardian deities of the common people of Zhen Dan. They possess extremely high [[img:icon_melee_attack]][[/img]]Melee Attack and [[img:icon_melee_defence]][[/img]]Melee Defence, and can use exceptionally powerful special abilities to shape the battlefield
Yellow Wind Ridge, eight hundred miles wide, once a fertile land beyond the pass—until a plague of rats rose from nothing, choking it in murky smoke, erasing all trace of human life.

[[img:icon_yang]][[col:white]]Unlock condition: Recruit Great Sage of the Yellow Wind into your ranks[[/col]]\\n\\nA volley of small explosives detonates in rapid succession, unleashing a devastating inferno.

The shields of the Rat Soldiers are imbued with the Great Sage of the Yellow Wind's magic; with a single gesture, they harden as solid as mountains, impervious to harm. But this spell only works once — once the magic fades, even the shield of gathered yellow sand crumbles away.

[[img:icon_yang]][[col:white]]Unlock condition: Recruit Great Sage of the Yellow Wind into your ranks[[/col]]\\n\\nThe Rat Overseers are the Great Sage of the Yellow Wind's most devoted followers; when facing death, they detonate the explosives strapped to their bodies.
The temples of Zhen Dan each master thirty-six external and thirty-six internal arts, but the Hao Tian Arhat has united every unrivaled skill into one being.

The Banner Troops carry flags emblazoned with the emblems of their respective garrisons upon their backs. As the vanguard of the assault, their banners will guide their comrades in the rear toward the point of attack.

Nan Gau's workshops teem with retainers summoned by Zhao Ming from every corner of the land — alchemists exiled to the desert, inventive craftsmen from the western empires; even the most outlandish designs have found patronage under the Bin Xi court. Zhao Ming's boldness has proven fruitful — the workshops have produced weapons and armor so fine that even the artisans of Kun Lan would gape in astonishment, and with them he shall forge an iron army for Zhen Dan.
The Guard Corps Soldiers form tight, disciplined ranks; beyond the tips of their blades, rivers of blood are sure to flow.
Wherever the Dark Spirit Army makes its stand, there Chang Yuan shall hold firm.

[[img:icon_yang]][[col:white]]Unlock method: Provide the frontier army with maximum aid at least once[[/col]]\\n\\nThe frontier armies form the primary defensive force of Chang Yuan, their ranks drawn from all corners of the land, reinforced with elite troops seconded from various courts. Some among them are the sons of noble houses, sent to Chang Yuan to serve in the ranks in hopes of redeeming past disgrace. Hardened by brutal war, these frontier soldiers bear a heavy burden, standing watch over the great yet weary nation behind them.
Let the frontier army shake, if it dares.
[[col:yellow]]The wearer has a very small chance of gaining a unique trait[[/col]]
The sword flashes like a shooting star, swift as lightning.
Sparse rain, sudden wind — even deep sleep cannot dispel the lingering wine.
Wherever the sword's clear light falls, iron melts to water and armor crumbles to dust.
The southern frontier shall never fall!

Zhen Dan's lands stretch vast and wide, and among its mountains, wilds, and marshes, demons and specters stir up calamity and ruin. Thankfully, wandering Daoist masters walk alone, rooting out these monstrosities and protecting the common people.
I am the dragon god's blade — born for this, and fighting until death.

In the age when the Dragon Emperor still walked among mortals, the Sky Sentinel Guards would be inserted alone into enemy formations, these frenzied warriors tearing mercilessly through the foe's defenses.
